item.title: Random Article Review #9, 17 October 2016
item.content:encoded:
An entry from the days when many of the entries were exercises in authors trying to make each other cringe at imagining the most fucked-up, horrifying thing possible happening to you. I'm not against that concept at all, even now, but after a thousand times it tends to lose a little impact. As the vote count would indicate, however, this seems to have been a successful execution of that era's expectations in that regard.

This tends to feature all of the trappings of the then-prevailing site writing practices, with the armed guards and the three dimensional chamber measurements and the what have you. It's also from a time when clinical tone wasn't nearly as standardized as it is now, so I read stuff like the following:

Test subjects have reported the pain of bonding with SCP-198 as a “searing” or “fiery” sensation

It was then that the nature of the SCP object revealed itself

And from a modern perspective, I cringe a bit, but I understand where it's coming from. It could definitely benefit from a cleanup with modern conventions in mind, though.

Where I really base my vote is in the presentation of the main idea, which is "how fucked up would it be if you had to drink an ever-refilling cup of your own bodily fluids constantly before you die." To be honest, I'd probably downvote the concept in any form, but the way in which this is written up, it feels excessively contrived and there's too many unnecessary elements.

By "excessively contrived," I refer to the following:

  • Bonds forever to your hands "at the molecular level" even if you happen to be wearing gloves
  • Gives you magical healing abilities so that even cutting off your hands doesn't help
  • Is indestructible1 so that you can't just break the container
  • Gives you magical malnourishment so that you can't do anything but drink your own pee or whatever
  • Teleports and disguises itself so that people can have the opportunity to mistakenly grab it and thus increase this thing's body count

This has a laundry list of stuff designed to basically force the reader to imagine a situation where they have to drink this disgusting thing over and over and there's nothing they can do about it, to the point of absurdity. It's almost humorous in that regard, but all it does in the end is blow past my personal Conservation of WTF threshold.

I find the addenda, the extended supplemental testing log, and the recovery sections to be filler. We already know, in great detail, what it does, and I'm not sure what I'm supposed to get out of it being randomly found in a German bunker somewhere, except maybe that I should be imagining Nazis forcing people to drink out of a magic transforming cup of grossness in a fit of Rube Goldbergian cruelty. The article already feels lengthy to me as I read it, and restating what I already know as a reader really bogs it down.

I imagine that there are people for whom this is their thing, and I think that it's possible to write that article in a far more elegant manner than what's on show here.

Footnotes
1. This is, by the way, a glimpse into the earlier origins of the "pointless indestructability" trope.

item.content:encoded:
Nice article and very evocative given the particularly rancid forms of death.

A big issue though - I don't get the [DATA EXPUNGED] parts. Each of them seems a little unnecessary, but the ones that I found really pointless were the two describing the contents of the cup. It has already said it is a bodily fluid, that it has been human saliva etc, so I feel there's no need to expunge anything.

Also, when you're talking about it's reappearance in various places, I feel the effect would be better if you preceded the [DATA EXPUNGED] with something. A word like inside, rupturing, causing the escape of/catastrophic etc.
You could do the same with the contents of the cup if you wanted to imply it was non-human, but if it is just human it is pointless to [DATA EXPUNGE] it.

Great article but will remain neutral to it unless that's changed I think. It just broke the flow for me.

item.content:encoded:
This is one of the best articles on the site by a good margin, in my mind. The thought of looking into a cup of vomit and knowing that you will be drinking that vomit for the rest of your short, pathetic existence before dying of thirst scares the crap out of me. The oh god it could be anywhere oh god factor is just icing on the cake.

That being said,

Site-██ with armed guards posted outside to prevent any unauthorized access.

Why on earth would anybody want to use this thing? If you're suicidal, there are certainly more pleasant ways of doing it.

Also, I think that disallowing any kind of cup or beverage holder at Site-██ and replacing them with hands-free drinking fountains would be a common-sense kind of thing.
